backward_compat_traps.rule: USB-PD negotiates power/role over the CC wire with BMC; it is NOT the USB 2.0 D+/D- data bus (NRZI, PID, endpoints, SOF).
backward_compat_traps.trap: Decoding USB-PD as USB 2.0 data (looking for D+/D-, NRZI, endpoints) is wrong — PD lives on CC.

backward_compat_traps.rule: USB-PD only negotiates power and roles; it does NOT tunnel USB 3.x / DisplayPort / PCIe at 20/40/80 Gbps like USB4 routers.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Treating the CC/VCONN pins as the USB4 high-speed tunneling fabric misses that PD is a low-speed contract protocol.

fields.spec_version: USB Power Delivery Specification Revision 3.1, Version 1.8 (USB-IF)
previous_versions: Thunderbolt 3 (2015, Intel) — donated base protocol for USB4.
USB4 Version 1.0 (August 29, 2019) — 20 / 40 Gbps router-based tunneling fabric.
USB4 Version 2.0 (2022) — adds 80 Gbps symmetric / up to 120 Gbps asymmetric (Gen 4, PAM-3).

key_changes.summary: Intel's 40 Gbps tunneling protocol over USB-C; donated as the USB4 base.
USB-IF tunneling fabric: USB3/DP/PCIe tunnels, router topology, Connection Manager, 20/40 Gbps Gen 2/Gen 3.
Gen 4 PAM-3 signalling for 80 Gbps symmetric; asymmetric (3:1) lane mode up to 120 Gbps; enhanced DP/PCIe tunneling.

fields.version_naming_history_note: USB4 is maintained by the USB Implementers Forum (USB-IF). Its base protocol is Thunderbolt 3, donated by Intel. USB4 1.0 was published August 29, 2019; USB4 2.0 (2022) added 80 Gbps. USB4 sits above earlier USB generations (USB 2.0 480 Mbps, USB 3.2 up to 20 Gbps) which it carries natively or via tunnels.

future_versions_industry_outline.summary: 10 Gb/s over 4-pair Cat 6a / Cat 7 UTP using LDPC + DSQ128 modulation; introduces Clause 55 PHY.
Adds Low-Power Idle (LPI) signaling for 100BASE-TX, 1000BASE-T, 10GBASE-T — Clause 78.
Introduces 40 Gb/s and 100 Gb/s over multi-lane fiber (40GBASE-SR4, 100GBASE-LR4, etc.) and Clause 81 XLGMII / CGMII.
100 Gb/s over backplane + twinax with FEC.
Single-pair automotive Ethernet PHYs sharing the same Clause 4 MAC.
Higher per-lane PAM4 rates targeting 800 GbE / 1.6 TbE.

lineage.summary: Original PD over VBUS using BFSK; superseded by CC-based PD.
BMC on the Type-C CC wire; Fixed/Variable/Battery PDOs.
Adds Programmable Power Supply (PPS / APDO), extended messages, fast role swap.
Extended Power Range up to 240 W (48 V at 5 A).
